subject.title: WhatsApp 1:1: inbound image wedges main lane ~3min before processing — multimodal run strands active_reply_work/queued_work_without_active_run (repro on 2026.6.10, post-#95039)

question: Should the WhatsApp direct-image active_reply_work loop stay as a separate fix target, or be folded into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97538 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99365 once that path has live/proven coverage for this trigger?
rationale: The source and related items overlap strongly, but this issue's updated repro is a distinct direct-image active_reply_work loop on a released build after earlier recovery fixes, so automation should not decide the permanent recovery-policy boundary alone.

options.title: Keep Separate Until Proven
options.body: Keep this issue open as a focused direct-image repro until current-main or post-PR proof shows this exact active_reply_work loop no longer wedges.

options.title: Fold Into Canonical WhatsApp Tracker
options.body: Close or mark this as duplicate only after maintainers confirm the canonical tracker and candidate PR explicitly cover the direct-image active_reply_work trigger.

options.title: Sponsor Recovery Policy Change
options.body: Use this issue to drive a narrower recovery-policy change for stale active_reply_work after terminal progress, separate from durable replay work.

recommendation.title: Keep Separate Until Proven
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as a focused direct-image repro until current-main or post-PR proof shows this exact active_reply_work loop no longer wedges.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant current code history is in diagnostic stuck-session recovery and lane release behavior.
